verifications.claim: "Integrity" is the official name given by the Artemis II crew to their Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Orion CM-003 Integrity[3]' 'named Integrity by the four-person crew.'; R3: 'The Artemis II crew members named their Orion spacecraft Integrity during a news conference Sept. 24.'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in multiple sources that the crew named their Orion spacecraft Integrity.

verifications.claim: "Integrity" represents trust, respect, candor, and humility, as well as the integrated efforts of NASA and the Canadian Space Agency.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'The name Integrity embodies the foundation of trust, respect, candor, and humility... nod to the extensive integrated effort... rooted in a shared core value of NASA... and the CSA (Canadian Space Agency).'
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to the description of the name's meaning, including specific values and agencies.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew successfully piloted Integrity around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R2: 'The flight was fully automated, and no crew intervention was required, though Wiseman would have been able to issue an abort command if necessary.'
verifications.reasoning: Mission was automated; manual piloting was only for specific tests, not piloting around the Moon and back.

verifications.claim: Integrity had a safe splashdown in the Pacific Ocean on April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'splash down off the coast of San Diego on Friday 10 April'; R2: 'Splashdown occurred April 11, 2026, 00:07:27 UTC (April 10, 5:07:27 p.m. PDT)... in the Pacific Ocean southwest of San Diego'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm safe splashdown in Pacific on April 10 local/PDT time.

verifications.claim: Integrity is the first crewed Orion spacecraft.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft, named Integrity by the four-person crew.'
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as the first crewed Orion flight.

verifications.claim: Integrity marks the first human mission beyond low Earth orbit since 1972.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'the first crewed flight beyond low Earth orbit since Apollo 17 in 1972.'
verifications.reasoning: Mission with Integrity explicitly described as such.

verifications.claim: Astronauts manually flew Integrity to test its capabilities.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Glover... took manual control of the spacecraft and performed a series of maneuvers'; 'Koch and Hansen took turns manually controlling the spacecraft to evaluate its performance'
verifications.reasoning: Specific instances of manual flying for testing described.

verifications.claim: Astronauts performed manual maneuvering to align Integrity for power generation during the 10-day mission.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the crew will manually drive the vehicle to centre the Earth... and then fly it to an altitude where the tail of the ship points towards the sun, so it can generate more power'
verifications.reasoning: Direct description of manual maneuver for solar alignment and power.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission lasted 10 days.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: '10-day lunar flyby Artemis II mission'; R2: 'Mission duration9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R3: 'approximately 10-day Artemis II test flight'
verifications.reasoning: Described as 10-day mission, but precise duration is 9 days +; broadly supported but not exact.

verifications.claim: The name "Integrity" was chosen to represent the core values and dedication of the thousands of people involved in the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'embodies the foundation of trust, respect, candor, and humility... the many engineers, technicians, scientists, planners, and dreamers... thousands of people across the world... Artemis campaign'
verifications.reasoning: Directly ties name to core values and thousands involved in Artemis.

verifications.claim: Integrity successfully handled the high-heat reentry.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Orion has the world’s largest heat shield... protect the astronauts from the extreme heat'; R2: 'Integrity re-entered Earth's atmosphere... before decelerating... Splashdown occurred'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm successful reentry with heat shield protection and safe landing.

verifications.claim: Parachutes deployed in sequence on Integrity to land in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Two small drogue parachutes... at an altitude of 25,000 feet... Three larger parachutes will slow Orion down even further... splash down into the Pacific Ocean'
verifications.reasoning: Exact sequence of drogue then main parachutes for Pacific splashdown described.

verifications.claim: Navy teams awaited in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'team to sea aboard the USS John P. Murtha... stationed "at a safe distance" away from Orion's landing place'; R2: 'U.S. Navy recovered the crew... USS John P. Murtha'
verifications.reasoning: Navy ships and teams positioned for recovery in Pacific.

verifications.claim: Integrity was officially named during a September 2025 news conference.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'named their Orion spacecraft Integrity during a news conference Sept. 24'; R2: '@NASA (September 24, 2025). "Integrity. That's what the Artemis II astronauts have decided to name their Orion spacecraft"'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm naming announcement on Sept. 24, 2025, via news conference and tweet.
